To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the supply of primary care is associated with better health, that having a relationship with a primary care physician is associated with better population health, and that receiving important features of primary practice is associated with better individual health and a more equitable distribution across population groups.
the health of populations is improved when they have a greater supply of primary care providers and when a greater proportion of the population has a relationship with a primary care source.
primary care helps to prevent illness and death and to promote health, and it does so in a more equitable way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the health effects of primary care, the health effects of health systems that include primary care, and the health effects of the features of primary care that are associated with health.
the contribution that primary care makes to the health of populations, the mechanisms by which primary care makes this contribution, and the policy implications of these findings.
the contribution of primary care to the health of populations and the means by which this contribution is made.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
primary care is an important contributor to health and health equity.
primary care contributes to the health and well-being of the populations that it serves.
primary care is a key component of a health system that improves health and reduces health inequity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
primary care, in contrast to specialty care, is associated with better health and a more equitable distribution.
primary care is an important contributor to the health of populations, and the more comprehensive and accessible it is, the better the population health.
primary care is a powerful and effective tool for improving health and reducing health disparities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
primary care has a positive impact on health and health equity and that the features of care that contribute to this impact can be identified.
primary care is a major contributor to health and health equity, and thus a major contributor to a healthy population.
primary care is a key component of health systems, and that primary care is associated with better population health, and with more equitable distribution of that health.
